questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISPUTE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

DISPUTE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Concede'. 

Key Points

  • The most appropriate antonym of the given word 'Dispute' is 'Concede'. 
  • Let's look at the meaning and examples of the words given in the Option:
  • Words Meaning Example
    Dispute an argument or disagreement, especially an official one between, for example, workers and employers or two countries with a common border They have been unable to resolve the dispute over working conditions.
    Concede to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true The government has conceded (that) the new tax policy has been a disaster.
    Strengthen to make something stronger or more effective, or to become stronger or more effective They have been strengthening their border defenses in preparation for war.
    Quarrel an angry disagreement between two or more people or groups They had a bitter quarrel over some money three years ago and they haven't spoken to each other since.
    Impute to say that someone is responsible for something that has happened, especially something bad, or that something is the cause of something else For purposes of the company's violations, the conduct of its officials and employees may be imputed to the firm.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DIVERSE
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

DIVERSE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Identical.

Key Points

  • The word "diverse" means showing a great deal of variety; very different. (विविध)
    • Example: The city is known for its diverse culture and traditions.
  • "Identical" refers to being exactly the same, or very similar. (समान)
    • Example: The twins were so identical that even their parents had trouble telling them apart.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'diverse' is 'identical'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Identical.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Parallel (समानांतर): Lines or planes that are side by side and having the same distance continuously between them.
    • Example: The two roads run parallel to each other for miles.
  • Practical (व्यावहारिक ): Concerned with the actual doing or use of something rather than with theory and ideas.
    • Example: He has a very practical approach to solving problems.
  • Farcical (हास्यास्पद): Relating to or resembling a farce, especially because of absurd or ridiculous aspects.
    • Example: The entire situation turned into a farcical comedy of errors.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PROVOKE

questions.solution: The correct answer is Conformist. 'Maverick' A person who doesn't conform to the norm. Example - The maverick artist challenged traditional art forms. 'Conformist'  A person who follows established customs or rules. Example - The company encourages employees to be conformists.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. His action doesn’t warrant such a punishment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

His action doesn’t warrant such a punishment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Breach'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate word antonym of the given word 'warrant' is 'breach'.
  • Warrant: an official written statement that gives somebody permission to do something. [(किसी काम को करने की) आधिकारिक अनुमति; वॉरंट, अधिपत्र, आज्ञापत्र]
    • Example: a search warrant [a document that allows the police to search a house]...
  • Breach: an act that breaks an agreement, a law, etc. (नियम, समझौते की शर्तों आदि का उल्‍लंघन; नियम-भंग)
    • Example: a breach of confidence...
       

Correct Answer: Breach.

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of other words:
    • triumph: a great success or victory; the feeling of happiness that you have because of this. (महान सफलता या विजय; सफलता या विजय का उल्‍लास)
    • support: to help somebody by saying that you agree with him/her/it, and sometimes giving practical help such as money. [किसी को (सहमति के आधार पर) समर्थन देना या किसी की (धन देकर) सहायता करना]
    • captivate: to attract and hold somebody’s attention. (किसी का ध्यान आकृष्‍ट रखना; मोहित कर देना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. The malice he developed for all caused a lot of damage.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

The malice he developed for all caused a lot of damage.
questions.solution: 'Malice' is a noun that means the desire to harm someone; ill will. Example: She recoiled inwardly at the malice in his eyes. 'Sympathy' means feelings of pity and sorrow for someone else's misfortune. Example: He expressed sympathy for his friend's loss.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Variance
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Variance
questions.solution: 'Variance' means being different, and inconsistent. Example: There is a variance in the test scores. 'Harmony' means a pleasing or orderly combination. Example: The colors in the painting are in perfect harmony.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. She has a penchant for art and craft.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

She has a penchant for art and craft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. 'hatred.'

 

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meanings of the given word and marked option:
    • Penchant- a liking for or a habit of doing something, especially something that other people might not like. (कुछ करने की आदत या पसंद, विशेष रूप से ऐसा कुछ जो अन्य लोगों को पसंद न हो।)
    • Hatred- an extremely strong feeling of dislike. (नापसंदगी की एक बेहद मजबूत भावना।)
  • ​Let's look at the meanings of the other given options:
    • Fear- to be worried or frightened that something bad might happen or might have happened. (चिंतित या भयभीत होना कि कुछ बुरा हो सकता है या हो सकता है।)
    • Joy- great happiness. (महान खुशी।)
    • Anxiety- an uncomfortable feeling of nervousness or worry about something that is happening or might happen in the future. (घबराहट की एक असहज भावना या जो कुछ हो रहा है या भविष्य में हो सकता है उसके बारे में चिंता करना।)
  • Hence from the given meanings, we find that ‘penchant’ and ‘hatred’ are antonyms.
  • So, the correct answer is option 1.

​

Additional Information 

  • Let's look at the synonyms and antonyms for the given word 'Penchant': (लगन)
  • Synonyms: affection, affinity, attachment, bias, liking.
  • Antonyms: antipathy, disinclination, dislike, hate, hatred.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Assiduous
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Assiduous
questions.solution: 'Assiduous' Shows great care, attention, and diligence in one's work. E.g. - The assiduous student always completes assignments on time. 'Idle' Showing a lack of activity, laziness, or not working diligently. E.g. - Instead of studying, he spends his time in idle pursuits.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ebb
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Ebb
questions.solution: 'Ebb' means the receding or declining of something, like the tide. Example- Consumer confidence is currently at a low ebb. The correct antonym is 'Flow' which means the steady movement or progress of something. Example: A flow of words is no proof of wisdom.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold in the following sentence. Her candid remarks impressed the Board of members.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold in the following sentence.

Her candid remarks impressed the Board of members.
questions.solution: 'Candid' means saying exactly what you think, genuine, etc. Example -She gave a candid response. 'Deceitful' means dishonest; trying to make somebody believe something that is not true. Example - I don't know how deceitful you can be with John.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Suffice
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Suffice
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Dissatisfy".

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given word.
    • Suffice: 
      be enough or adequate.
      • Example: Basita said, "I don't think the food we had ordered will suffice the guests."
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options.
    • Excessed: more than the usual, proper, or a specified amount.
    • Immatured: not fully grown or developed.; deficient in maturity; lacking wisdom, insight, emotional stability, etc.
    • Satirize: 
      deride and criticize by means of satire.
    • Dissatisfy: 
      fail to satisfy (someone).
       
  • As per the meaning of the given words, "dissatisfy" is the antonym of the word "suffice".
    • Example: The waiter did not want to dissatisfy the customers so he lied that the food was freshly made.
​Hence, the correct answer is option 4.​

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. His poems are recondite in subject matter
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

His poems are recondite in subject matter
questions.solution: 'Recondite' is Difficult to understand or obscure. Example - The professor discussed recondite theories. 'Simple' Easily understandable or uncomplicated. Example - The instructions were simple and clear.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Precocious
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Precocious
questions.solution: 'Precocious' Showing advanced development or maturity at an early age. Example - The precocious child started reading at three years old. 'Backward' Slow to develop or learn. Example - The child was a bit backward in terms of language skills.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Impudent
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Impudent
questions.solution: Impudent means very rude; lacking respect and not polite. Example: The boy was punished for his impudent behavior/attitude. Polite means having good manners and showing respect for others. Example: The assistants in that shop are always very helpful and polite.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. There are some technologies available today that make a notebook dispensable .
questions.questionHtml:

There are some technologies available today that make a notebook dispensable.
questions.solution: 'Dispensable' Able to be done away with or not essential. Example - The extra decorations were dispensable for the party. 'Essential' Absolutely necessary or indispensable. Example - Good communication is essential for a successful team.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word Comely
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word

Comely
questions.solution: 'Comely' means pleasurably conforming to notions of good appearance, suitability, or proportion. Example: The garden looked comely in the warm morning light. 'Grotesque' means a very ugly or comically distorted figure. Example: It was something grotesque, but definitely not a skeleton.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Reinforce
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Reinforce
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Weaken. 'Reinforce' To strengthen or support. E.g. - The additional evidence will reinforce their argument. 'Weaken' To make something less strong or less effective. E.g. - The continuous exposure to harsh weather will weaken the structure over time.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Frustrate
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Frustrate
questions.solution: 'Frustrate' To prevent from achieving a goal or desire. Example - The constant delays frustrated the team's efforts. 'Foster' To encourage or promote the development of something. Example - The company aims to foster a culture of innovation.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Accessory
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Accessory
questions.solution: 'Accessory' Something that is added to another item to enhance or complement it. Example - The necklace was a beautiful accessory to her outfit. 'Essential' Absolutely necessary or indispensable. Example - Oxygen is essential for human survival.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Amiss
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Amiss
questions.solution: 'Amiss' is Incorrect or not as it should be. Example - Something seems amiss with the calculations. 'Impeccable' Perfect and without any flaws. Example - Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the event.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Objurgation
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Objurgation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, Endorsement.

Key Points

  • Objurgation means a harsh rebuke or criticism.
    • For example, "The coach's objurgation of the team's poor performance was heard throughout the locker room."
  • Option 1, Hamper, means to hinder or impede progress.
    • For example, "The heavy rain hampered the construction workers' ability to finish the project on time."
  • Option 2, Reproof, means a mild rebuke or criticism.
    • For example, "The teacher's reproof of the student's behavior was met with a sincere apology."
  • Option 3, Commination, means a threat of punishment or retribution.
    • For example, "The company's commination of legal action against the competitor was taken seriously."
  • Option 4, Endorsement, means approval or support.
    • For example, "The celebrity's endorsement of the new product led to a significant increase in sales."
  • Overall, the opposite of objurgation is endorsement, as one is a harsh criticism while the other is a positive approval.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Adequate
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Adequate
questions.solution: 'Adequate' means sufficient or satisfactory in quantity, quality, or performance. Example: The meal was 'adequate', but not particularly memorable. 'Wanting' means lacking or deficient in something. Example: The restaurant's service was wanting, as the waiters were slow.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Inept
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Inept
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Competent.

Key Points

  • "Inept" and "Competent" are opposite to each other because they represent contrasting levels of skill, ability, or proficiency.
  • "Inept" is an adjective that describes someone or something as lacking skill, ability, or competence. It suggests a lack of proficiency, effectiveness, or suitability in performing a task or fulfilling a role. In Hindi: अयोग्य
  • Competent: Competent means having the necessary skill, ability, or knowledge to perform a task or fulfill a role effectively. It refers to being capable, proficient, or skilled in a particular area. In Hindi: योग्य
  • As we can see, the meanings of both the words are opposite to one another.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Competent.

Additional Information 

  • Wanting: Wanting means lacking or deficient in some aspect, often referring to something that is insufficient, inadequate, or not meeting the desired standard. In Hindi: अभावपूर्ण
  • Barred: Barred means being obstructed, excluded, or prevented from accessing or participating in something. It involves being prohibited or restricted from entry or involvement. In Hindi: निषेधित
  • Callow: Callow means immature, inexperienced, or lacking in sophistication or understanding due to youth or inexperience. It refers to being naive or undeveloped. In Hindi: अनाड़ी

questions.question: Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the word given below. Wane
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the word given below.

Wane
questions.solution: 'Wane' To decrease gradually in size, intensity, or power. E.g. - The moon's brightness will wane after the full moon phase. 'Intensify' To become stronger, more intense, or increase in size or degree. E.g. - The storm's fury will intensify as it approaches the coast.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Delinquency
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Delinquency
questions.solution: 'Delinquency' refers to the act of failing to fulfill one's obligations or responsibilities. Example: His repeated delinquency led to his expulsion. 'Fulfillment' signifies the act of meeting or completing obligations or responsibilities. Example: The employee's prompt and efficient work ensured the fulfillment of all project deadlines.

questions.question: Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the word given below. Relentless
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the word given below.

Relentless
questions.solution: 'Relentless' means to be persistent, unyielding, or unrelenting in one's actions or efforts. Example: Her pursuit of justice was relentless and inspiring. 'Intermittent' refers to something that occurs at irregular intervals. Example: The intermittent rain showers made it challenging to plan outdoor activities.

questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word. Forthright
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Forthright
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'Uncandid'.

Key Points 

The word that is opposite in meaning (antonym) to "forthright" is "uncandid."
Forthright: The word "forthright" means to be direct, honest, and straightforward in speech or behavior.
Uncandid: It means being not open or sincere, lacking frankness or honesty.(अच्छी तरह से बात न करने वाला)  This is the correct antonym for "forthright."
Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Uncandid'.

Additional Information

  •   Explanation of the other options:
    • Artless: This word means lacking skill or cunning, without artifice or deception.(अकुशल)
    • Uninhibited: This word describes someone who is free from social constraints or inhibitions, openly expressing their thoughts or feelings.(निराविधिक)
    • Blunt: This word refers to someone who is straightforward or direct in speech, often to the point of being rude or lacking tact.(कुदरती)
